hook_formula: High-stakes supernatural rule hook: Stating an absurd, impossible condition ('Every boy who asks my crush out gets struck by lightning') paired with immediate visual proof (boy holding flowers getting zapped) and escalating personal consequence ('I've been struck 11 times').
story_arc: Setup (supernatural curse on crush striking suitors with lightning) -> Escalation montage (protagonist attempts asking her out with rubber suit, car, bucket, bleacher spectators, hospital visit) -> Detective revelation (discovering the cloud is sentient and in love with her) -> Creative resolution (wingman play: building a pink fog machine girlfriend for the cloud) -> Romantic success & comedic punchline (crush says yes, dad still misses his fog machine).

visual_style.background_details: Roblox high school exterior with warm yellow brick facade, modern glass windows, neatly trimmed trees, stadium grandstands filled with NPC spectators, cafeteria lunch benches, and rooftop overlooks.

source_transcript: Every boy who asks my crush out gets struck by lightning. I've been struck 11 times. I'm asking her out if it kills me. It's come close. The first time I just asked. My eyebrows grew back in March, so I wore a rubber suit. It melted. I asked from inside my mom's car. Now my mom drives a convertible. I wore a metal bucket on my head. They saw that one from space. By the eighth time, the school was selling tickets. Everyone said she was cursed. She ate lunch alone. Under an umbrella. The dance was Friday. My doctor said one more bolt and my hair would stay like this forever. Then I looked up. It was the same cloud every time. When she went to camp, it cried for a week. It wasn't a curse. The cloud was in love with her. You can't beat a cloud, so I found it a girlfriend. I put my dad's fog machine on the roof. Love it first sight. I asked her again, not a single bolt. She closed her umbrella and said yes. The cloud and the fog are still together. My dad wants his fog machine back.
